title: Onboard eval cross-kernel contrast report — 2026-07-12
content:
Purpose:
This note collects the cross-kernel behavioral diffs we observed when onboarding model: rwd-open-13b-v2 under three runtime permutations: (A) flash-attention enabled, paged-KV disabled, standard batching; (B) flash-attn disabled, paged-KV enabled, continuous-batching disabled; (C) flash-attn enabled, paged-KV enabled, continuous-batching enabled. The goal is to summarize signal across our canned onboarding promptset, call out regression classes, propose prioritized mitigations, and give a recommended rollout policy for Dedicated and Hosted lanes.

Quick executive summary (TL;DR):
- Net quality delta is small on mean metrics (perplexity, exact match), but there are concentrated failure modes when paged-KV and continuous batching are active together: hallucination spikes on long-context instructions, and token-level latency jitter that cascades into timeouts for streaming clients.
- Flash-attention alone (A) shows improved p50 token latency (-12%) with no measurable semantic regression across our eval promptset; keep enabled for perf.
- Paged-KV enabled alone (B) reduces memory pressure but introduces subtle prompt-truncation artifacts for prompt templates that rely on deterministic prefix casing; manifests as punctuation dropouts in ~0.7% of generative responses.
- The full stack (C) uncovers an interaction: KV page eviction schedule + continuous-batching request coalescing occasionally serve stale KV slices to follower requests, creating incoherent continuations. Frequency: 0.14% of requests across the long-context benchmark but 1.9% of failing examples in the onboarding abstraction tests.

Test matrix and datasets used:
- Model: rwd-open-13b-v2 (onboard candidate)
- Promptsets: onboard_shortform_v1 (instructions <256 tokens), onboard_longform_v1 (>512 tokens, multi-turn), eval_regression_smoke (targeted corner cases: numeric reasoning, list formatting, code blocks)
- Hardware: p4d-24xlarge-like (A100-style), quantization: 4-bit q4f16 for candidate baseline, identical across runs
- Runtime permutations: A (flash=on, pagedkv=off, contbatch=off), B (flash=off, pagedkv=on, contbatch=off), C (flash=on, pagedkv=on, contbatch=on)
- Metrics: token-p50/p95 latency, end-to-end response time, perplexity on heldout, top-1 semantic accuracy (task-specific), hallucination rate (annotator), formatting regressions (regex-based checks)

Aggregate numeric highlights (delta relative to baseline A):
- flash-only (A vs baseline-oldruntime): token p50 -12%, p95 -6%, perplexity +/-0.4%
- paged-KV only (B vs A): memory footprint -28%, perplexity +0.9%, punctuation-dropout rate 0.7%
- full stack (C vs A): end-to-end p95 latency +18% (due to batching coalescing spikes), hallucination rate +1.2% (absolute), failing-example rate on onboarding_longform_v1: 1.9% vs 0.2%

Concrete examples (redacted):
- Case 17231 (onboard_longform_v1): multi-turn math problem. Expected: stepwise reasoning and final numeric answer. Observed (C): model repeats partial reasoning then outputs an unrelated concluding sentence referencing previous conversation context from other request. Root cause signal: KV page mismatch; evidence: KV page id in logs (kv_page=0x7c3f) differs between request start and follow-up chunk.
- Case 19402 (eval_regression_smoke): code-block formatting lost closing backticks when paged-KV was on. Batches that spanned a page boundary showed truncated trailing tokens.

Investigation notes and logs to inspect:
- We captured request traces with kv_page ids and batch-coalescing traces in /tmp/onboard-traces-2026-07-12.tar.gz (linked artifact above). Key log patterns: "evict_page" events that occur during an active request window and "batch-commit-delay" spikes correlated with specific host nodes.
- Repro recipe: run longform prompt with --trace-kv and --batch-window=8ms on variant C; reproduce failure ~1 in 500 local runs. Increase batch-window artificially and failure probability rises to 1 in 120.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race between page-eviction and continuous-batching merging (high confidence): when a leader request causes an async eviction and a follower's coalesced request reads from the same page id before page refresh, stale KV slices are used. Evidence: matching timestamps across "evict_page" and "serve_chunk" logs.
2) Flash-attention's cache layout changes expose alignment assumptions in the paged-KV accessor (medium confidence): some pointer arithmetic assumes contiguous KV layout. Evidence: pointer delta aligned with flash-attn kernel memory strides in crash dumps.
3) Prompt-tokenization edge cases expose different caching keys (low confidence): minor tokenizer normalization differences produce additional KV page splits.

Short-term mitigations (fastest to deploy):
- Roll back continuous-batching by default in Hosted for rwd-open-13b-v2 until fix verified (rollback toggle: CONTBATCH_FALLBACK=enabled). Scope: Hosted only; Dedicated customers can opt-in with nurse flag.
- Harden page-eviction to be request-aware: prevent evict_page events for pages in-flight (safety patch), add small grace window (50ms) during leader/follower merges.
- Add detection: log and increment a metric when a batch-served request references a page id different from leader-request start; raise a P1 alert when rate >0.05% on onboarding sets.

Longer-term fixes and tests to run before re-enabling on Hosted/general rollout:
- Ensure atomic KV view switch for coalesced batches: implement versioned page pointers so followers see consistent snapshot during coalesced execution.
- Add unit tests that inject delayed evict_page events into the coalescing path and assert no stale pages are readable.
- Add integration test to onboarding harness that runs 10k long-context prompts with contbatch enabled and asserts failure rate <0.25%.

Recommended rollout policy:
1) Patch (safety) + monitoring (2 days): enable in Dedicated staging with contbatch off by default for ongoing onboard candidates.
2) Canary (1-2 weeks): enable contbatch + paged-KV together for 5% of user traffic routed to an isolated pool with additional tracing and automated rollback on metric breach (hallucination rate and kv-mismatch metric).
3) Full enable: only after integration test pass and observed failure rate <0.25% on long-context harness for 72h.

Open action items (owners):
- Miguel: add kv-mismatch metric + Grafana dashboard (due 2026-07-16)
- Priya: implement safety-grace-window patch in evict logic and add unit tests (due 2026-07-18)
- Tom: expand onboarding harness to 10k long-context runs and run overnight once patch applied (due 2026-07-19)
- Lena (owner): coordinate Hosted rollback and customer communications draft (due 2026-07-15)

Notes to reviewers / unresolved questions:
- We need product guidance on whether Dedicated customers should ever have contbatch gated behind a strict opt-in; some larger customers rely on contbatch for throughput. I'm leaning to an opt-in with strong monitoring and a documented escape hatch.
- Does quantization profile interact with paged-KV eviction frequency? A quick test showed small differences; we should capture traces under q8 and q4 to be sure.

Appendix A — sample prompt fragments from failing examples (sanitized):
- "System: You are a step-by-step math assistant. User: Calculate 17*43 showing all steps. Context: <many previous steps>"
- "User: Combine the following code snippets into a single function. Make sure you include closing backticks.
```python
def helper():
    return 3
```
"

Appendix B — quick grep queries to triage locally:
- "grep -R \"evict_page\" /var/log/redwood | grep <request-id>"
- "jq -r .kv_page trace.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr"

Appendix C — quick timeline of events captured:
- 2026-07-10: initial onboard run with flash-attn only — no anomalies
- 2026-07-11: paged-KV experiment introduced in staging — observed punctuation-dropouts
- 2026-07-12: contbatch added in integration — spike in hallucinations and kv-mismatch signals
- 2026-07-13: extended runs and root-cause triage; hypothesis 1 formed

Informal notes / scratch:
- I ran fuzzer over the tokenizer and saw a handful of edge cases around "\u2019" and hyphenated tokens that cause token-count jumps. Might be unrelated but file under follow-up.
- Customer impact estimate: small absolute fraction but affects high-perceived-value flows (long multi-turn assistants) — prioritize fix.

If you need repro scripts or raw traces ping me in #applied-ml-onboarding (Slack) or see linked artifacts above.
